body:
Ok to sum up the discussion so far:

* \#2289 was created because it's inconsistent to tell the users they can use their input, and then force the original state on it even if it has a value itself
* there is an edge case: when there are two searchboxes there is an inconsistent visual state. It happens when one of the searchbox is not providing an input with a value. This is an edge case in a context of an edge-case and we'd be happy to work on it if a user has the issue.

As a side note, this feature (using an input instead of container) is a very early one. Nowadays it can be done with the connectors. This should probably be removed in the next major version.

Can we move forward with this PR @vvo @iam4x ?
